item.title: Almost 1,000 arrests in protests across France
item.description: A coalition of the “Yellow Vests” movement, trade unions and students will march across France on Saturday with demands over studying conditions and purchasing power. Some 70,000 police are expected to be deployed as authorities fear looting and vandalism similar to last Saturday's unrest. Publicado también por: France 24 - English. Fuente: ABC News Australia.

item.title: Infantino claims support of 'vast majority' of soccer ahead of FIFA elections
item.description: Views may be split over the future of the FIFA president, but football's biggest powerbroker claims he has "vast, vast majority" support ahead of his re-election bid. Fuente: ABC News Australia.

item.title: 36er knew his NBL days were numbered when he had the 'most pain ever'
item.description: Isaac Humphries, who shocked 36ers fans this week by announcing he was retiring from the NBL, opens up on the injury that forced him into a decision that "wasn't really mine in the end". Fuente: ABC News Australia.

item.title: 'Eyes moving west': Sydney's new airport opens to passengers today
item.description: "Eyes are moving west" when it comes to forward-planning for the future growth of Western Sydney and its new airport, which opens to passengers today. Fuente: ABC News Australia.

item.title: Labor pitches $1.5 billion plan to slash emergency wait times

item.title: Some regions still climbing as nation sees record drop in house prices

item.title: Kim Jong Un crosses new bridge into China as trade ties warm
item.description: North Korean leader travels over New Yalu River Bridge to meet senior Communist party member Kim Jong-un has visited China, inaugurating a bridge that connects the two countries and saying he hopes to expand cooperation with his neighbour. The North Korean leader arrived in the Chinese border city of Dandong on Saturday after crossing the New Yalu River Bridge, according to South Korea’s unification ministry, which handles affairs related to North Korea, and China’s official Xinhua news agency. Continue reading... Publicado también por: The Guardian - World. Fuente: ABC News Australia.

item.title: The extraordinary discoveries emerging from the ruins of Juukan Gorge
item.description: Archaeologists have found a huge trove of extraordinary artefacts preserved in the arid soil at Juukan Gorge, years after an ancient rock shelter within it was destroyed by a Rio Tinto blast. Fuente: ABC News Australia.

item.title: Trump's waning support among young men could hurt Republicans

item.title: The Tasmanian garden helping people with dementia live well
item.description: A gardening program in Hobart is helping people with dementia reconnect with the world around them. Researchers hope the lessons from these outdoor spaces will help more people continue to live well. Fuente: ABC News Australia.

item.description: Cricket great Usman Khawaja could barely walk and thought he had a terminal illness when he was just starting out his Test career. He was soon diagnosed with a crippling disease, which he has kept secret for 17 years. Fuente: ABC News Australia.

item.title: The BoM’s temperature record keeping is under attack – again. What’s going on? | Temperature Check
item.description: An ‘audit’ of the Bureau of Meteorology main dataset for measuring climate change claims it contains ‘widespread errors’. It doesn’t stack up Want to get this in your inbox when it publishes? Sign up for the Clear Air Australia newsletter here Australia’s climate has warmed by more than 1.5C since 1910, according to the Bureau of Meteorology’s main long-term temperature data. If you were so motivated, you might think if you could discredit this data, then you would undermine the whole climate change story and even – perhaps – the rationale for cutting Australia’s greenhouse gas emissions… Fuente: The Guardian - Environment.
